utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I again remind you, hopefully for the last time, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Lukic will now continue his re-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would try to find things moving faster, and I would like to have two documents on our screens at the same time. If possible, I would like to have 1D05544 on the left-hand side of the screen. It's the picture. And 1D01405 on the right-hand side of the screen. It's a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the transcript, we need page 35, please, in the e-court, and that should correspond to transcript page number 7846. We need the last line on this page and then we'll move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, we talked about this yesterday, you remember, the incident in the Klare Cetkin Street. That's G-6.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were present when Mr. Sabljica marked this photograph. I will now read out what happened at that trial session, line 25 on this page: [In English] "Thank you. Can you now please tell us whether this measuring band was placed in the way that you would place the band to indicate the major axis? "A. Yes, but we did mark all the traces and based on the photograph it is my assumption that this could be indicating the direction from which the projectile had come in." Line 10 and further now: "The Accused: [Interpretation] Could the witness just please mark -- could he just mark the outer-most pockmarks, the fragment traces, and then we can go back to the photograph. So can he just sort of put a circle around the farthest marks. "The Witness: [Interpretation] Well, that's what we can see in the photo at least. "Mr. Karadzic: [Interpretation] "Q. Thank you. "The Accused: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please sign this document. "Judge Kwon: Just for reference, could you circle the power-plant just to be clear." And then we should move to another page, the next one. Line 3: "A. Oh, I see. Here, T for 'toplana,' heating plant. "Judge Kwon: If you could put the date, your signature, and then we will admit it as Exhibit D755." [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, do we see on this photograph what Mr. Sabljica marked?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When the discussion was about the measuring tape, where is it on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the middle of this imprint that the shell made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this picture into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document 1D5544 receives Exhibit Number D1279, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have 10570 on our screens. The problem with this document is I think that one version is in English and the other one is in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There is no B/C/S version. [Interpretation] So it's 22nd January 1994. This is Captain Verdy's report, the UNPROFOR report, dated 22nd January 1994. Can we now see page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did Verdy find? From how many weapons was fire opened?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From one weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you agree with Verdy on this?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same finding we put in our report. That's what all the investigation pointed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there anything in this report that you didn't agree with?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on the traces left by the shell on the asphalt, we concluded that we [as interpreted] confused the azimuths with the points of the incident in Klare Cetkin Street. Otherwise, he wouldn't have been able to write what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- the transcript now reads that "we confused the azimuth," but I take it that it is "he confused the azimuth with the points of the incident." Is that -- yes, I see the witness is nodding in the affirmative. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 29137, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we move on to a different exhibit, if counsel could just check whether the last one, the Verdy report, I believe it's already admitted as D178.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was trying this morning. I couldn't find if it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With a B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: D sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D178, I did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- hear you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it? It is. We have just checked it is. Thank you. Now if we can move to 29137, 65 ter number, please. This is statement Borislav Stankov gave to the OTP in 1995. And we will need the next page in both versions, please. I'm trying to locate in English version, it's the second paragraph from this last line in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the B/C/S reference to the Vase Miskina, 27th of May, appears in the English on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the previous page. No, in English previous page. Maybe it's uploaded wrongly, or can we try with a third page?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can see by the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a two-page document in e-court, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In -- in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so the order couldn't be the problem, but the completeness of course is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see just by the ERN range that there is multiple pages missing from the uploaded part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll read one portion we want to address only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- would you have the -- for us the -- the 65 -- any 65 ter number so that at least we have an opportunity to at least look at it for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2913 -- oh, yes, but if it's uploaded incompletely then that doesn't help. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankov says here: "When we determined the directions of these two shells, we found the crossing point at Nedzarici. That's an area under control of the aggressor, 500 or 600 metres from the spot. The first shell came from the west, the second shell, 82-millimetres, came from north-west (original unclear)."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in my -- my impression is that we didn't have the B/C/S version on the screen with respect to what you read. Where can we find it? Then we should go to the next page in English. It must show up there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We tried. There is only two pages in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, did Mr. Stankov determine the origin of fire in the same way as you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. Using the same method.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, how many mortars were there according to him?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to him as well, there was one mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In what way did you differ from Mr. Stankov?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we differed in the individual origins of fire of these shells and the type of shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm a bit lost here. First of all, could you lay a foundation for -- because what -- from what you read, I'm not saying that it's not in the document, which we can't verify it, from what you read it doesn't say anything about how the origin of fire was determined. So could you please check with the witness. It only says that it was determined, not how it was determined, so we do not know what the knowledge -- on what the knowledge of this witness is based, that's one. Second, I'm also a bit puzzled by the fact that you just read about a first shell and a second shell and then -- oh, that's how many mortars, yes. I withdraw that last observation. But could you please inquire with the witness what's the basis of her knowledge. And if Mr. Weber has anything to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in addition to the points that you just observed, I have been able to catch up and locate, in the English version at least, for us to read along. And I see that Mr. Lukic picked up in a mid-part of a sentence which actually includes some context about the two shells that are being discussed in the part then referred to by Mr. Lukic. So I ask just that if counsel is reading in the information, that he reads the full sentence or information related to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, normally we would leave that to the other party to deal with it later, but if you have not provided us with the English version of the portion you read, you are hereby invited to follow the suggestion by Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I read the full sentence. There are sentences before that, of course, and I was interested merely in how many mortars and which method was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is how many mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean tubes or do you mean shells?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tubes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mortar --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tubes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tubes, yes, okay. That wasn't entirely clear right from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I can clarify that with the witness, Your Honour, where can we see it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, where would you like, for context, Mr. Lukic to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At least in the English it appears to be punctuated as one sentence. But it starts with: "I wrote down direction of the Institute of the Blind because the 82 ..." I don't know if counsel sees that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to read that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I wrote down that the direction was the Institute for the Blind because two 82-millimetre shells landed on both ends of a long building with 100 to 150 metres between them. When we determined the direction of these two shells, we found the crossing point at Nedzarici. That's an area under the control of the aggressor, 500 to 600 metres from the site. The first shell came from the west, the second 82-millimetre shell came from north-west (original unclear)." From which part --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just have a -- does it say "north of west" or "north-west"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says "north-west." And in brackets it says the original is not clear. So if you have English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, where do we see here that these two shells were fired from one tube?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this passage in the text where the witness says that after determining two directions of descent of the shells, he found they crossed at one point, and that tells us that both shells were fired from one tube, from one mortar. And according to his findings, that was by the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see on the screens 1D05927.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would you please, during the break, take care that you find or agree that we have a full picture of this paragraph of which you read some parts. Because I see reference is made to 120-millimetre as well, so there must have been more than just 82. You can't fire 120-millimetre mortar shells from 82 tubes, so therefore it's a bit confusing for us being unable to read the whole of the paragraph. So if you please take care of that, then you may proceed now. Unless Mr. Weber has a good reason to stop you from proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If it would expedite things, this individual is the individual who authored one of the reports, and I see from the portion that you may not have in front of you that he's discussing his report in the matter. So to the extent that this information may overlap with the actual report before the Chamber, that -- that I believe is what the witness is commenting on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we have before us is a compilation. This is something we did over the last few days. This is a combination of figure 30 from 1D05948 and -- that's your paper on mortars, and page 10 from P00644. You were asked about co-ordinates. The co-ordinates that were entered, that Captain Houdet marked in his report. We overlapped the meridians, and that can be seen easily on meridian 90, so it's easy to follow. This is what I would like to ask you now: The scale of the map, this map, or any map, does it affect the position of co-ordinates on a map?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Co-ordinates are one and the same, irrespective of the scale of the map, and they are the ones provided by Captain Houdet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just offer this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5927 receives Exhibit Number D1280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, it was my understanding that the issue was that there were two different systems of grid scales there, not about the scale. So therefore, I fail to see what it brings us. But it goes without saying that if there is a grid scale on a map, if you enlarge it or if you zoom in, then of course you zoom in the grid scale as well. The issue was the grid scales are not same on the map you plotted compared to what was plotted contemporaneously. That was the issue. So therefore -- well, Mr. Weber didn't object, but it doesn't address the gist of the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, if measuring systems are changed from mils or 6.000, 6.400, 360 degrees, would these differences affect determining the wrong co-ordinates on this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That also is not the issue. But if you want to continue on matters which are not what was -- then please, if you want to use your time in that way --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just to add on, it's getting a little leading at times too, and so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But apart from that, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Chamber would be assisted by properly addressing in re-examination matters that were raised as problematic in cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask you something about incident G-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we need on our screens is a document of the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, 33202.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that this is the document. Have you found this in your paper? The Prosecution said that this document is related to the incident in Cane Babovic Street on the 12th of July. Further down you can see the order: Urgently at 600 hours on the 13th of July, 1993, at the latest, continue Operation Lukavica 1993 as per tasks received. Further on: Liberate the Trnovo-Kijevo-Sarajevo road as per priority in order to provide units with necessary materiel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we please scroll down in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile I put on the record that this document has been admitted as P7556. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Trnovo-Kijevo-Sarajevo, that road, does it have anything to do with Dobrinja? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, it has nothing to do with Dobrinja. As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you briefly about incident G-9. This is page 146 in B/C/S and 150 in English, your paper on mortar attacks in Sarajevo. My colleague Mr. Weber put a few things to you there as well, and he said that you did not correctly describe the testimony of Mr. Ekrem Suljevic. That part is on 155 of the B/C/S version and 160 in English. And you said in your paper the witness, Ekrem Suljevic, did not explicitly state why in these photographs the damage on the walls had not been marked or circled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you give the 65 ter number? Because Madam Registrar doesn't know what the paper on mortar attacks is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And at the same moment, I would like to correct the transcript. Page 14, line 25, the number should be P7556. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now if we go to page 155 in B/C/S and 160 in English, so we need 155 in B/C/S. We have -- it's second paragraph on this page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that Ekrem Suljevic did not explicitly state why in these photographs the damage on the walls was not marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 65 ter 33156. That is the testimony of Mr. Suljevic in the Karadzic case on the 6th of September, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 1 of this document, line 21 onwards. [In English] I quote: "How do you explain that there are some markings on the shutter, most probably marked by chalk, whereas we see now no damages inflicted by fragments on the wall? "A. I wouldn't dare claim that, based on this photograph. If we were to examine it more carefully, we may be able to find some damages but" - then we move to the next page - "they aren't marked. But the narrative under the photograph says that the purpose of this photograph was to show the damage done to the metal shutter." [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, when you were there on the spot, were there any -- was there any damage on the scene -- on the wall that could indicate that it had been caused by explosions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the same incident, my colleague Mr. Weber also put to you that you did not properly convey what Witness W-12 said, namely, whether there were two explosions or just one explosion, the one that he heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but if counsel is moving away from the -- Mr. Suljevic, it's just not clear. I -- I would be inferring that she's not referring to the photograph or Mr. Suljevic's testimony in her answer, but it's not clear to me. It should be referring to what she saw when she visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- that's the impression I gained as well, but perhaps you could clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What -- I just wanted to emphasize that even Mr. Suljevic said it may be able, "we may be able," and it's not explicit. That's what we wanted to say. And Mr. Weber said that it's not correct and that he explicitly said that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, that really wasn't just the point of my comment. It was just -- to explain why he was doing it. It was just to clarify for the record what the witness was referring to, whether she was referring to the photograph or her own observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I can -- I can try to clarify with Ms. Subotic this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but let's then start right away with what Mr. Weber put to the witness exactly, and then to see where in her report, because that's what we are talking about, she reflected that accurately. Because its seems that the response to your question was what she found on the spot, which of course is not the same as what she wrote in her report. That's apparently the issue at stake. If you could clarify that, that would be appreciated. But I leave it in your hands whether you wish to do that, yes or no, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Ms. Subotic, what was your understanding of this? Would you change something now, now that you've seen all of this and what we read out today? Did Mr. Suljevic explicitly say something about the damage or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he did not say anything explicitly about the damage. And it is based on photographs from the photo documentation. We checked that. The situation is the same as it was in the photo documentation; that is to say, there are no traces. And we saw what he said exactly. And I believe that he did not say anything explicit about the traces on the wall, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So I'm going to go back to this again. My colleague Mr. Weber also put it to you that you did not properly convey the testimony of Witness W-12 in terms of whether there were two explosions or just one explosion, the one that he heard. You speak about that in paragraph 95 of this report of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05498. Let us take a look at this. We'll have it on our screens. We need paragraph 95. [In English] It's a big report, so probably it takes some time to upload. Now we have. And now we will -- in B/C/S version we need page 146, and then we will move to 147 later. And in English version, we need page 151. And if we can have B/C/S version on the left-hand side as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have two English versions. Yes. That's paragraph 95. Then we move to the next page in B/C/S, please, to page 147. Now, we have two B/C/S. Okay. I'll move on. We don't have time for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your report in paragraph 95, you said that Witness W-12 could not confirm that he heard the firing and the other explosion, the second explosion.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Lukic please slow down and repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my colleague Mr. Weber put it to you on transcript page, in our trial, 39718, line 6. This is what we'd like to read out now. "Q. First of all -- you are going on, but that's not what I said. And I would put it to you, actually, that we -- W-12 heard two shots. I don't want to engage in a long debate with you about it. We have his statement in the investigative file where the witness indicates two firings." [Interpretation] So first of all, let us look at what Mr. Weber put to you. The statement that Mr. Weber spoke of, it is in the document, and we need it on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D01259. [In English] Not to be broadcast, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see it's been taken care of. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, we are not going to mention any names. The name of this man, that is. Thank you. We have the document on our screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 11 in B/C/S, and in the English version page 7. The B/C/S version is barely legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is not a statement. This is an official report, an Official Note. And the witness who is mentioned here did not accept this Official Note as his own, so I'm showing this to you just so that you'd know what I'm talking about. Now, let us take a look and see what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would be appreciated if counsel could just proceed to questions if there is information --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- as opposed to informing the witness of such --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- misstatement of the evidence on the -- Mr. Weber's side. I'm surprised that he is insisting on this. This is not a statement and it's not signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a piece of evidence before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you should know what this is, not what Mr. Weber said it was -- it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can ask the witness whether she knows better, but you shouldn't testify yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ask the witness what she reads in the document, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, please use the English version as well because the B/C/S version is barely legible. In your view, is this a statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is written here is "Official Note." That much I can read from this document that is totally unclear and illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you see who signed it? Was it signed by the person that supposedly signed this because that person's name is written here?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. Lukic, that we are entering the area of what the legal meaning of all this is. And then we are easily confused by the evidentiary value of an Official Note in the system in which such a note was prepared or what that means for being in evidence before this Chamber. I would not expect the witness to know anything about it, but if you think it is, then please lay a basis for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Now we need the document on our screens 1D05 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move to another document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- you asked this witness about the signature, and you should clarify. She said: "I would say no," to your question was it signed by the person whose name --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's hard because I cannot mention the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, whose name appears in the document, at least in the English version. The witness said she supposed that this is not the signature of that person. I think you should clarify it further, what is the basis for this impression by the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think it would certainly help if you clearly referred to what person you are referring to, the person providing the information or the person who has drafted the Official Note. Apparently you are not -- you are not clear in that respect if you talk about a person. So if you want to clarify it, please do so but in clear wordings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, what is marked on the document, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In B/C/S, I cannot -- sorry, sorry, I thought that you had finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The person to whom these words are ascribed, these words in this Official Note, is mentioned as someone, at least in the English version that is legible, as someone who signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's just what I wanted to say. On the basis of the English version, the person that is mentioned is not referred to as the signatory of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about this? There is no dispute about it, Mr. Lukic. I don't know what you are doing. These questions that it's signed not by the person who gave the information is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is in dispute? I didn't understand it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then -- let's -- you try to find out. This is not in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never mind. 1D05730. Could we see that on our screens. We have a transcript before us of the testimony of Witness W-12 on the 2nd of March, 2007, in the case against Dragomir Milosevic. In this transcript, we need page 32 in e-court, and it should correspond to the transcript page 3077 from the Dragomir Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From line 16 on this page, we can read out the following, what this witness said, under oath, during a trial before this Tribunal. [In English] I quote: "Q. I would like to ask the witness this: Who gave you the idea of there having been a second round, the other round being fired? "A. Nobody gave me the idea. We heard this over the radio that people had been injured. By the time I got home, one of my neighbours said, Two shells have landed on Bascarsija. People have been killed and wounded, and that's where the two shells come in. I myself don't remember there being two shells. I know about the one that came from Trebevic. Now, as to Vidikovac and that sort of thing, it was probably from somewhere around there and it landed at Bascarsija." [Interpretation] Is this the statement that you had in mind when you wrote your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now in addition to this, could we please have two documents again on our screens. And it's different documents from the one that we have on our screens now. One is 1D05731. This is like photograph 90 from your paper. And parallelly, I would like to have another document on our screens.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Lukic please repeat the number of that document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05729.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This witness marked the map when he testified on 1st March 2007 before this Tribunal, also in the Dragomir Milosevic case. You referenced it in your footnote 381 about mortar shells -- shell attacks in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document on the left, in the transcript, we need page 78 in e-court. In fact, we can move on straight to page 79. It should correspond to page 3037 in the transcript, line 3: [In English] "Q. Thank you very much. I see that the map is now on the screen. Witness, do you see the map on the screen? "A. I do." Mr. Cannata now tries to zoom in. And line 8, I quote: "... at the time of the shelling incident, you stated that you heard a sound of a shell when you were on your way to the front line; is that correct? "A. Yes. It was in the area of Brajkovac. "Q. Very well. Would you be able to mark, with the electronic pen that Mr. Usher will kindly provide you with, the area that you just indicated on the map. And if you need it to be zoomed, just tell us. "A. Yes, this is where Brajkovac is. "Q. Can you put a small A, a letter A, within that circle. "A. [Marks]" Now we have to go the next page. Line 16. Where you -- "Q. Very well. Did you see where these shells landed? Where did it impact? "A. No, I did not. The weather was bad. But we assessed that it was the old part or the old quarter of Bascarsija. "Q. Can you mark this -- this quarter on the map in front of you, as you did with the circle. Can you circle that area. "A. [Marks]. "Q. Can you put a letter B within the circle. "A. [Marks]" And then we need the next page, line 10: "Q. Would you be able to locate on the map the location which corresponds to the direction of the sound you heard that day? In other words, what you think is the place where the shell was fired. Can you mark it. "A. Yes, I can. It's the Vidikovac area. "Q. Can you put a letter C within the circle you have just marked. "A. Yes. "Q. Thank you." And if we go three pages ahead, we need transcript page 3042. And we see that from line 13 to line 22, this witness was marking his brigade, 115. And he marked it with the letters 115 -- with numbers 115 and letter B.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, we've seen that you referenced this photograph and the testimony of this witness. At the very end when you've reviewed everything, how did you understand his evidence, that he heard one or two explosions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the end of the day I understood that he heard one explosion and that's what he said. In fact, he heard one firing and one explosion. That's how I understood him and that's how we treated his evidence in our report after all this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know it's break time and I will stop now. I will just offer this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we take that break, you stopped reading somewhere where I saw on the next line that the witness was talking about shells in the plural rather than in the singular.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you -- can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, it moved immediately away, but I'm seeking perhaps your or Mr. Weber's assistance in finding the spots where the witness was apparently talking about shells. But again, I had no opportunity to read it, but it was just following a portion you did read. And therefore, I'd -- I would be assisted if you would take care of that. Meanwhile, we will decide on admission of this document as ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wait for the parties to give context and -- but for the time being, is there any objection against the map at the time marked by the witness to be admitted into evidence? If not, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5731 receives Exhibit Number D1281, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honours, we checked the transcript of W-12, and we found no mentioning in plural of mines or shells by him, only by the lawyer who posed the question on page 3038, line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He posed the question in a plural way, but then corrected himself and put it in a singular. And the next one is on 3041, line 7, also singular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of the problems if you have to follow it very quickly. I appreciate your assistance. If Mr. Weber disagrees, then we'll hear from him. And whatever he needs for context, of course, Mr. Weber, you can apply for adding that. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, on page 39772 of the transcript in our case, Mr. Weber asked you if you had ever used the Cymbeline radar. [In English] I will actually read so we know I don't miss anything. So in line 9, it starts with a question, I quote: "Q. You have never operated a Cymbeline radar system; correct? "A. That's correct. "Q. You do not know that these Cymbeline radar systems can be pointed in different directions known as arcs; right? "A. Yes, I know that. I read reports compiled by UNPROFOR." [Interpretation] Now I'll show you one document to see where the Cymbeline radar was directed on 28th August 1995 at the time of the Markale incident at the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need 65 ter 05703.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what questions will follow, Mr. Lukic, but of course it's usually not that you -- if the witness can clarify any matter which is in there, that's fine, but of course not to establish what it was or was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And is this document in the witness's report? If I could have that section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. You could ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't need this document, so obviously either the number is wrong or I misspoke. Give me one second. That's the number I have with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could first ask the witness whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 1D -- sorry. Now I can see. It's 65 ter number 1D05703, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge as to where the Cymbeline radar was directed on the 28th of August, 1995, at the time of the Markale incident? We are talking about Markale II. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. And we cited it in our report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you'll forgive me for not having all the footnotes on the top of my head or to remember all of the thousand pages by heart. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Still if counsel could direct me if this document is referred to, just so I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that we can see what was cited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see it's in -- that it's footnote 477 in Markale --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the Markale report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- report, yes. It's 1D05496. Page 196 in B/C/S version. But we have another document, different document in front of us, and I will deal with that document. We need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that document referenced in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document we're looking at --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it's on 127, page 127 in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have before us the statement that Mr. Bleakley gave to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. We need in B/C/S page 12 and in English page 10. In B/C/S we need the second paragraph from the bottom, and in English the fourth paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "The tables give you the height with different charges. We combined this information with the ceiling of the Cymbeline radar. I think that we came to the conclusion it could have been two gunpowder charges. The radar was looking at that part of the city. "The second charge would have cut the beam. We then went to the Cymbeline radar. Warrant Officer 2nd Class Andy Harries was the Warrant Officer in charge. He took me to the back of the radar. I went with Powers. He showed me the arc on the map that the radar was looking at. At 170 degrees or 240 degrees a shell would have cut the beam - Gunner Rooney was the operator in the back of a vehicle. He was glued to the screen. This was within two hours of the impact. He was at the airport looking east. He had to have a high elevation for some reason -- terrain? But he said nothing had broken the beam." So you told us that you cited this, but did you take into account this fact stated by Warrant Officer Bleakley -- by Major Bleakley?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, our analysis are consistent with what he stated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought I heard a fact, but are you talking about facts or -- because there are a lot of facts in that statement. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did -- I appreciate that I did ask some general questions about Cymbeline, but then I think I -- if I recall my examination correctly, I went very specifically to a chart that was in her -- a photo and the origin of that information. That was kind of the point of the cross-examination. I believe Your Honour even admonished me about it, me calling into question that it's not to scale and where it said it. I'm not sure that this is in the report. I read the exact text that was just read out. At this time, really, I don't think -- after all these hours, re-examination should be -- just be used to -- when I ask a basic question or two to establish the personal knowledge or lack thereof of a witness, as a basis to then launch into further evidence that should have been led on direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, exactly. That's why I read -- read portion. I didn't change anything, but I read the portion from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But Mr. Weber said about the -- he was discussing directions in which this radar can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- pointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can be. The difference is that Mr. Weber dealt with the matter in more general way, whereas you're focusing now on a specific thing. But I wouldn't stop you there at this very moment, but please keep in mind the limited time we have. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said your report agrees with this. Will you tell us what exactly in your report is consistent with this observation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said you agreed with these statements of Major Bleakley and that they conform to what you found. Could you just tell us what exactly in your report is corroborated by this statement by Major Bleakley?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this part that relates to the determination that the second charge would cut the Cymbeline beam and all the others, of course. Although he didn't deal with that. So he said the second charge would cut the beam. That's the same conclusion that we came to, whereas the first charge would go under the beam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. Witness, Mr. Lukic read to you: "He was at the airport looking east. He had to have a high elevation for some reason - terrain? But he said nothing had broken the beam." Could you tell us what does that mean: "He had to have a high elevation for some reason"? What does that mean in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He obviously had to set up the radar in such a position so as to have it cover the critical parts of the trajectory, and the radar had to be in such a place so as to cross all the six trajectories with its beam. That's a position that he had to ensure in order to be sure that he would catch everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what should have been and what was may not necessarily be the same. What was the -- how was the beam in vertical -- in vertical direction, how was that -- how was it? Do you know? Because I do understand that if you have a system, you can move to the left, you can move to the right, you can move a little bit up, you can move a little bit down. Do you know how this Cymbeline radar at that moment was installed or -- do you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's written in the statement with just the red; that's to say, at 170 or 240 degrees, a shell would cut the beam, said the gunner. Those are the azimuths that were investigated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But high and low. I mean, I do understand these are compass bearings. But do you know whether -- what the ceiling exactly was, how it was at that moment installed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's stated here that a second charge would certainly cut the beam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question. I mean, whether or not it would have cut the beam depends on how it was -- the beam was directed, vertically and horizontally. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly agree with this, but we are just reading a statement that says how the beam was directed. And it says that azimuths 170 to 240 would certainly cut the beam and all the charges from 2 upwards would also certainly cut the beam. There is no reason to discuss technical possibilities and options when we have a specific statement saying how it was actually directed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we don't have such a statement. We have a conclusion by someone who may have known how it was directed. He said on a charge 2 it would have cut the beam. That's a conclusion. That's not exactly -- we don't know on what exact given information that conclusion is drawn. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that they took information from the area where they were and then they came to a conclusion on that basis and on the basis of the firing tables. Otherwise, we practically do not have any conclusions, exact technical ones, anywhere in this entire case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's still to be seen. But, Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we -- are you done with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. If you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to go to the last page. I don't see any signature or affirmation. On the first page it was said that this was a draft, which was not signed. I just state that for the record. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we will be able to locate the signature, so if you have anything else. But -- I'll continue in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, did you see anywhere in any UNPROFOR report that it was recorded that this beam had been cut in any other report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All reports made attempts to see how the shell went underneath the radar beam.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about incident G-10. That's the one in Aleksa Santica Street number 50. It's air bombs. The 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5497, page 47 of the B/C/S version and page 46 in the English version. Incident G-10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, were you contesting the fall of an air bomb there in Aleksa Santica 50?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you contest that that bomb had arrived from the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is the size that was being contested. That is what my colleague Mr. Weber had put to you.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just -- we might be confusing two instances here. G-10, I believe, has a different date, not the 1st of July, 1995, at a different address than Aleksa Santica number 50. So I think that we're conflating some incidents in questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you check, Mr. Lukic, whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have it marked as incident G-10. And it's -- it's dealt with in this report on modified air bombs at page 138 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: G-10 is on the 7th of April, 1995. I see the report discusses that date clearly, and I believe that the questions now have confined of conflated different things that I asked related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- two separate incidents on two different dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would say you are talking about another G-10 than Mr. Lukic is doing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think the cases talked about a different G-10 than what Mr. Lukic is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.text: At transcript page 39862, you discussed how you resolved issues of perspective in photographs. You were asked: "Q. All right. utterances.text: I meant specifically the resolving of the problem in the Vase Miskina Street, putting the photograph in an orthogonal position. It's a very standard programme.
