utterances.text: Your Honours, with that, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Lukic, as I said before, you have an opportunity to revisit the -- and the Chamber will listen to any objections coming in not later than the 19th of October. Then I would have only one or two small questions for the witness in relation to the minimum angle of descent of shell in front of the city market-place which she provided to us. Do we still have a clear copy of that that could be put on the ELMO? I have one but there are a few notes on it. Madam Registrar, could this be given to the usher and could it be put on the ELMO. Is it visible to everyone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the diameter of the shell you took into consideration, the diameter was how many centimetres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the diameter of the -- that's the whole of it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that half of the diameter was taken into account that should be taken so that the shell would not rub off the edge of the roof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's -- therefore you say --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the radius. Not the diameter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The radius is 6 centimetres and I think we talked about that. At least that's what I see in the transcript. Now, your first calculation, you corrected it by -- you said: CSB, security services centre, it would be 11.45/4.8 = 67.25. And now you take into account the calibre of the shell. And your next calculation is 11.45/4.76. I'm puzzled by -- I'm puzzled by that because I thought you would deduce 6 centimetres rather than 4 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. I made a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, a lot has been said about mistakes these days. Thank you very much for -- I don't see any reason to have it in evidence with the mistakes which are in there. Therefore, the Chamber refrains from doing anything with it at this very moment. Thank you for that answer. This concludes the testimony of you, Ms. Subotic. I would like to thank you very much for being with us a long time, coming from a long way. Distance is always important, isn't it. And for having answered all the questions that were put to you, both by the parties and by the Bench. And I wish you a safe return home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Procedural. You said you had approximately half an hour of deliberations today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, deliberations not, but to deal with all kind of matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have one urgent decision which I would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see it's -- is it break time already or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's almost break time. I have a very short, that means 3 minutes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Why I'm asking is whether I should propose that we do not start Mr. Poparic only because of five, ten minutes at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I even wonder whether we can go through all of our matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let's try to -- no, Mr. Poparic is -- is not expected to begin his testimony today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I would read one decision before the break and then deal with quite a few other matters after the break. The decision is a decision on the Defence motion to admit the evidence of Witness GRM125 pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The Chamber will deliver this decision now. It's a decision on a motion filed on the 7th of September, 2015, to admit the evidence of Witness GRM125 pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I add to this that a tendered associated exhibit is already in evidence. In its motion, the Defence submits that the witness offers relevant and probative evidence in relation to the historical, political, and military background of events in the municipality Kotor Varos, specifically the activities of the municipality's civil protection staff and its sanitation platoon, as well as refuting claims by Witness RM009 on these matters. In its confidential response of the 21st of September, the Prosecution opposes the motion. While it accepts that a small part of the proffered evidence relates to the historical, political, and military background of events in the municipality of Kotor Varos, it argues that the majority of the statement constitutes a judgement on the credibility and reliability of Witness RM009, usurping the role of the Chamber and making the evidence unsuitable for admission pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The Chamber recalls and refers to the applicable law in relation to the admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Rules as set out in previous decisions. The parties do not specifically dispute the relevance or probative value of the tendered evidence. In relation to the Prosecution's objection, the Chamber considers that the statement contains numerous conclusions about Witness RM009's evidence without providing a factual basis. The credibility attacks does appear to be very personalised instead of focusing on factual descriptions of events. Under these circumstances, pursuant to Rule 92 bis (A)(ii)(c) of the Rules, the Chamber considers that it is appropriate that the Prosecution be given an opportunity to test or clarify the witness's candid attacks on Witness RM009. For these reasons, the Chamber finds that the witness should be made available for cross-examination if the Defence wants to present the proffered statement as evidence. Accordingly, the Chamber denies the Defence's Rule 92 bis motion and invites the Defence to indicate within one week from the date of this decision whether it wishes to reinstate the Rule 92 ter motion which had been filed for this witness at an earlier date. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. We take a break. We'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00 -- to 2.00, and then deal mainly with procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will deal with a few procedural matters. I'll start with delivering a few decisions. The first one is a decision on a Defence motion which was filed on the 31st of August, 2015, to admit the evidence Witness GRM162 pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In its motion, the Defence submits, inter alia, that the witness offers relevant and probative evidence in relation to military courts and military judiciary investigations. According to the Defence, the proffered evidence directly relates to crimes alleged in counts 1 to 8 of the indictment. The Defence submits that the witness's evidence relates to the historical, political, and military background of events in Sarajevo and is largely descriptive, therefore weighing against calling the witness for cross-examination. In its response of the 14th of September, the Prosecution opposes the motion on two grounds. First, it submits that the tendered statement is misleading as its content has been clarified and sometimes contradicted by the witness's testimony in the Karadzic case. In view of the nature and number of the differences between the statement and the witness's Karadzic testimony, the Prosecution considers that tendering additional material from the witness for contextualisation is, in this instance, not a viable remedy to the one-sidedness of his statement. Secondly, the Prosecution submits that the witness's tendered evidence relates to a live and important issue in this case weighing in favour of denying the motion. It submits that the evidence relates to the military justice system which represented one way in which VRS soldiers could have been punished for crimes, thus directly relating to the accused's alleged command responsibility and contributions to the alleged joint criminal enterprise. The Chamber recalls and refers to the applicable law in relation to the admission of evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis of the Rules as set out in previous decisions. The parties do not specifically dispute the relevance or the probative value of the tendered evidence. In relation to the objections by the Prosecution, the Chamber is concerned that the Defence apparently takes statements of witnesses without ensuring that any corrections or clarifications made in prior examinations are included. The possibility for the opposing party to add contextualisation to the tendered material is one safe-guard to avoid receiving one-sided evidence. However, adding portions to the contextualisation can also reach a level where it is more efficient to have the witness come to court as opposed to trying to understand various sources of contradicting evidence. More importantly, having reviewed the submissions of the parties, the Chamber considers that Witness GRM162's evidence on the military justice system relates to a live and important matter in this case as the military justice system's functionality is directly relevant to the means available during the indictment period to, inter alia, the accused. The Chamber considers this to be a factor weighing strongly against granting the motion. Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the witness should be made available for cross-examination if the Defence wants to present the witness's evidence. Accordingly, the Chamber denies the Defence's motion and invites the Defence to indicate within one week of this decision whether it wishes to reinstate the Rule 92 ter motion which had been filed before for this witness, that is, before at an earlier date. And this concludes this Chamber's decision. I move to my next decision, which is a decision on the admission into evidence of associated exhibits tendered through Witness GRM130. On the 8th of September, 2014, the Defence filed a motion tendering a witness statement and 13 associated exhibits through Witness GRM130 pursuant to Rule 92 ter of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. On the 12th of February of 2015, at the invitation of the Chamber, the Defence filed a submission withdrawing three of the 13 associated exhibits. The Prosecution filed its response on the 26th of February, not opposing the admission of the ten remaining documents. The Chamber recalls that documents can be admitted as associated exhibits if they form an inseparable and indispensable part of the witness's written testimony. In order to satisfy this test, the tendering party must demonstrate that the witness's statement would be incomprehensible or of less probative value without the admission into evidence of the associated exhibits. The Chamber has discussed its interpretation of the applicable case law at transcript pages 530 to 531, 5601 to -03, and in its written decisions of the 23rd of July, 2012, and the 7th of February, 2013. The Chamber considers that some of the documents are needed to properly understand the statement and that a denial would result in the statement having less probative value. The Chamber therefore finds that each of these documents forms an inseparable and indispensable part of the statement and admits documents bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 1D02872, 1D02873, 1D02894, 1D02912, and 31148 into evidence. As the Prosecution is still seeking the authority of the Republic of Serbia to publicly use document bearing Rule 65 ter number 1D02895, the Chamber admits it provisionally under seal and will await submissions from the Prosecution in this regard. The Chamber finds that the four remaining documents are not discussed by the witness to such an extent that they form an inseparable and indispensable part of the witness's statement, and therefore denies admission of documents bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 1D02635, 1D02874, 1D02893, and 1D03736 into evidence. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to file a memorandum assigning exhibit numbers to the admitted documents. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I now move to delivering the Chamber's decision on the admission of a military notebook marked for identification as P7321 during the testimony of Branko Basara, pending, inter alia, additional submissions by the Prosecution concerning the document's provenance. On the 20th of May of this year, the Prosecution filed additional submissions regarding P7321. The Defence did not respond. During Basara's testimony, the Defence challenged the authenticity of the document and raised a general objection against the admission of, and I quote, "any documents received by the AID." I refer to transcript page 34492. The Chamber recalls that the applicable law for the admission of evidence is set out in Rule 89(C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which allows a Chamber to admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value. Document P7321 concerns a 72-page military notebook which was provided to the Prosecution through the BiH Agency for Investigation and Documentation, or AID. In its 20 May submissions, the Prosecution requests that only a five-page excerpt of this notebook, as put to Witness Branko Basara, is admitted into evidence. This excerpt has been uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 31873a. The Prosecution further provides detailed submissions on how the notebook is cumulative of other evidence admitted in this case. The Chamber is satisfied that the excerpt bearing Rule 65 ter number 31873a is relevant, inter alia, to the charges concerning the municipality's component of the indictment. It is cumulative of other evidence admitted in this case and has probative value within the meaning of Rule 89(C) for the purposes of its admission into evidence. Lastly, the Chamber considers that the document's probative value is not outweighed by the need to ensure a fair trial pursuant to Rule 89(D) of the Rules. In this respect, it notes that the Defence has not provided information as to why the document's source, the AID, would render it unreliable and, more importantly, how its unreliability is reflected in the document itself. For these reasons, the Chamber admits the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 31873a into evidence as Exhibit P7321. The Registrar is instructed to replace the B/C/S original and corresponding English translation, currently uploaded in e-court under P7321, with the documents uploaded under the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 31873a. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on document P7321. I move on, and I start with a remaining issue from the testimony Dragic Gojkovic. During the testimony of Dragic Gojkovic between the 10th and the 12th of August, 2015, D1171, D1172, and D1184 were marked for identification pending communication of a revised English translation for D1171, of the English translation for D1184, and of the revised B/C/S original and English translation for D1172. Furthermore, D1183, Gojkovic's expert report, was marked for identification pending agreement between the parties on the parts of the expert report to exclude. On the 14th of September, the Chamber e-mailed the Defence to ask for an update about these exhibits. As of today's date, the Defence has not provided any update. The Chamber gives the Defence a dead-line of one week from today to update the Chamber. I now move to a remaining issue from the testimony of Goran Krcmar. It's about D918. During the testimony of Goran Krcmar, D918 was marked for identification pending receipt of the English translation. On the 15th of April, 2015, the Defence advised the Chamber, via an e-mail, that CLSS believed that the original document was actually in English and therefore they suggested that the Defence contact ICMP for the original English version. The Chamber understood that the Defence expected to receive the document in May. The Chamber e-mailed the Defence on the 21st of August and the 11th of September to ask for an update, but as of today's date, the Defence has not provided an update. The Chamber gives the Defence a dead-line of one week from today to update the Chamber. The next item is a remaining issue from the testimony of Ewan Brown about P2930. On the 28th of August of this year, the Prosecution informed the Chamber, via e-mail, that a revised English translation of Exhibit P2913 -- I said -- I think I pronounced 13, but I meant "30," that is therefore P2930, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0113-9110-ET. The first question is whether there is any objection from the Defence? I take it that you need more time for that, Mr. Lukic. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the English translation of Exhibit P2930 with the document bearing doc ID 0113-9110-ET. And, Mr. Lukic, you have until the 19th of October to express any concerns and make any submissions in relation to this matter so then to revisit it. Next item is about P7532 and P7277. On the 2nd of September of this year, document bearing 65 ter number 11377a was marked for identification as P7532 under seal. On the same day, the court officer informed the Chamber via e-mail that the number P7277 was reserved for this excerpt on the 30th of March. This is to be found on transcript page 33855. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to vacate Exhibit Number P7277. On the 28th of September, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that the revised translation, under doc ID R103-0361a-1-BCS has been uploaded into e-court. Same question, Mr. Lukic, whether there is any objection to the newly uploaded translation. You again have a -- until the 19th of October to revisit this matter if you wish to do so. Meanwhile, we'll proceed. A question to the Prosecution is whether P7532 needs to be admitted under seal. Any reasons? You're all alone, Mr. Tieger. I see that -- well, not all alone, you're assisted, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it appears to us that there is no such reason when we look at our records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't know whether the Chamber raised the inquiry for a particular reason that we should follow-up on and we're happy to do so if that's the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it was marked for identification under seal. That's the reason why. That's at least my information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. And based on the nature of the document, the manner in which we received it, the witness involved at the time, we simply can't see a basis. It looks -- it appears to us to be a public UN document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, since the exception needs reasons and not the ordinary, which is public, the Chamber hereby admits -- yes, Mr. Lukic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this the one that I have to respond until 19th of October? You gave that dead-line to me before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. No, I think that's another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because the same document, 75 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see, that it's -- the objection is to the translation. Yes. But as we usually do, we decide on admission, although you can revisit the translation issue. But of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the other question is in view of protective measures and in view of admission itself whether you have any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not at this moment. Then the Chamber hereby admits P7532 into evidence. I move on to the next item, which deals with Exhibit P474. On the 28th of April of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that a revised English translation of Exhibit P474, which is a VRS Main Staff order dated the 6th of June, 1992, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0362-9105-0-ET, and the Defence responded the next day advising that it did not object to the translation being replaced. The Chamber therefore hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P474 with the new one of which I just read out the doc ID. I move on to my next item, similar in kind, about Exhibit P4005. On the 12th of May of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that there was an error in the e-court upload of Exhibit P4005, a Prijedor municipal assembly decision dated the 31st of August, 1992, in that the second page was missing. A corrected version of Exhibit P4005 was uploaded under doc ID 0190-4149-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old version of Exhibit P4005 with the corrected one, and the Defence has an opportunity until the 19th of October to revisit this matter. I now move on to Exhibit P3045, similar matter. On the 9th of June of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that the revised English translation of Exhibit P3045, a decision of the Bijeljina wartime commission dated the 17th of September, 1992, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0090-3110-ET. The original translation referred to the members of the war commission in the Ugljevik municipality which was not in the B/C/S original. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P3045 with the new one and gives the Defence one week, or let's say until the 19th of October, to revisit the matter. Next item, perhaps doesn't come as a surprise, also an English translation replacement, now in relation to Exhibit P3794. On the 11th of June of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber advising that a revised translation of Exhibit P3794, a Republika Srpska MUP article, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0220-1005-1-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P3794 with the new one and gives the Defence until the 19th of October to revisit the matter. Yes, I think there was one number which I may have pronounced unclearly. The newly uploaded revised translation of P3794 was uploaded under doc ID 0220-1005-1 ET. I now move to the next one, unless, Mr. Tieger, you want to interrupt me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, at some point we need to -- and I think this is the best opportunity. We need to return to a previous matter raised, and, in fact, I would ask to do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Earlier today P7532 was admitted. The status is hereby changed. P7532 is admitted under seal. I move to the next item which is P379 -- no, I have dealt with that one already. I move on now to Exhibit P41, which deals not with the replacement of an English translation but the replacement of a B/C/S translation. On the 30th of March of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber advising that a revised B/C/S translation of Exhibit P41, an UNPROFOR situation report dated the 6th of July, 1995, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID R111-3217-BCST. In the original, the entry for 03.15 to 03.22 at the top of page 5 referred to rockets, whereas the previous translation referred to "projektila." The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P41 with the new one. I think I said to replace the old translation with a new one and gives the Defence until the 19th of October to revisit the matter. Next item deals with Exhibit P1247, again English translation. On the 23rd of February of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that a revised English translation of Exhibit P1247, an intercept dated the 12th of July, 1995, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0107-7909-1 ET. The previous English translation of the intercept says that: "At 1920 there was no carrying signal," whereas the original reads "1900." The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P1247 with the new one and gives the Defence until the 19th of October to revisit the matter. Next item deals with Exhibit P3307. On the 16th of February of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber advising that a page was missing from Exhibit P3307, admitted under seal, and that the corrected version had been uploaded into e-court as document bearing 65 ter number 30602a. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old version of Exhibit P3307 with the corrected version and gives the Defence until the 19th of October to revisit the matter. I move to what most likely will be the last one I can deal with today, which deals with P7260. On the 27th of March of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that a revised English translation of Exhibit P7260, a Drina Corps command order, had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0436-7186-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P7260 with the new one and gives the Defence one week -- and gives the Defence until the 19th of October to revisit the matter. To the extent I would have forgotten that, and most likely I did, Mr. Tieger, I'm -- P7532 gives repetitious problems. I think that the English translation newly uploaded should replace the old translation and the -- Madam Registrar is hereby instructed to do so. Not to say that my agenda is empty, there are quite a few remaining issues, but we have no further time. We adjourn for the day. We'll not sit next week. Therefore, we'll resume on Monday, the 19th of October, 2015, 0930 hours, courtroom I. And I already announced to the parties that most likely on the 20th of October we'll have a bit of a shorter session that we'll conclude earlier than the usual quarter past 2.00. I think it would be likely at approximately 12.00. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of October, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
